sentences.text:
----
 2/ 22.02.2018 Heard learned counsel for the parties.
Learned A.P.P. appearing for the State opposes the prayer for bail of the petitioner.

Petitioner is an accused for allegedly committing an offence punishable under Sections 11(a)(d)(e)(i)
& (k) of Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960, Rule 3 of the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (Slaughter House) Rules, 2001, Section 55 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and Sections 429, 406, 188 and 120B of the Indian Penal Code.

entities.text: Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960
entities.label: STATUTE

entities.text: Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (Slaughter House) Rules, 2001, Section 55
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Some camels were entrusted to this petitioner before Bakrid, which were not produced by this petitioner at later stage.
It was presumed that this petitioner and others have slaughtered the said animals.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is absolutely innocent and has not committed any offence.
He submits that the petitioner is in custody since 10.01.2018.
In view of the aforesaid fact and keeping in view the nature of allegation, I am inclined to grant privilege of bail to the petitioner.

Accordingly, petitioner, Akhtar Ansari, is directed to be released on bail on furnishing bail bonds of Rs.10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand) with two sureties of the like Akhtar Ansari vs The State Of Jharkhand ...
